title: Kingdom of Powys Fadog
capsule: Powys Fadog was the northern portion of the divided Kingdom of Powys, formed after Madog ap Maredudd's death in 1160 split the realm between his descendants. His son Gruffydd Maelor I held the northern lands including the cantref of Maelor and commotes of Yale and Glyndyfrdwy from around 1160 to 1191, and his successor Madog ap Gruffudd (1191–1236) gave the sub-kingdom its eponymous name ('Fadog' deriving from 'Madog'). The attestation window 1169–1216 covers Madog ap Gruffudd's consolidation of the realm, during which he initially maintained neutrality between the Welsh princes of Gwynedd and English power before allying with Llywelyn ab Iorwerth by 1215. Powys Fadog survived through the thirteenth century as a client of Gwynedd until Edward I's conquest; the 1284 Statute of Rhuddlan abolished its remaining autonomy, and its lords' descendants included Owain Glyndŵr.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political outline of Powys Fadog is reasonably attested in Welsh chronicles and English administrative records, but the cantref-level territorial boundaries are reconstructed from medieval surveys and carry moderate uncertainty.
